wholeQuestion.question: A screening pathway must be introduced to entire hospital wards, so allocating it to individual patients is impractical. Which design best evaluates its effect on patient centered outcomes among these options?
choices: A pragmatic cluster randomized implementation trial
A cross sectional survey of tool preference
A case report of one positive screen
A laboratory assay validation without patients
wholeQuestion.rationale: Randomizing wards matches the level at which this pathway is delivered. The trial must address recruitment bias, spillover between wards, and clustering in its analysis; cluster randomization does not guarantee clinical benefit or eliminate contamination.

choiceReview.choice: A pragmatic cluster randomized implementation trial
choiceReview.assessment: Ward randomization matches an intervention that cannot be allocated to selected individuals.

choiceReview.choice: A cross sectional survey of tool preference
choiceReview.assessment: A preference survey does not test patient outcome effects of the pathway.

choiceReview.choice: A case report of one positive screen
choiceReview.assessment: One case cannot estimate comparative pathway effects.

choiceReview.choice: A laboratory assay validation without patients
choiceReview.assessment: An assay study without patients cannot evaluate this clinical pathway.

wholeQuestion.question: Which analysis best handles repeated weights nested within patients across hospital units?
choices: A chi square test without time
A case series with no model
wholeQuestion.rationale: A longitudinal model should account for repeated observations within patients and clustering by unit. Its covariance structure and treatment of unit effects must fit the study and number of units; a random unit effect is not automatically appropriate when there are few units.

choiceReview.assessment: A multilevel longitudinal approach can represent the repeated-patient and unit structure, with model assumptions checked.
An unpaired test alone ignores the repeated and clustered structure.

choiceReview.choice: A chi square test without time
choiceReview.assessment: A chi-square test without time does not model the serial weight measurements.

choiceReview.choice: A case series with no model
choiceReview.assessment: An unmodelled case series does not address the stated correlation structure.

sourceLocations: Jakobsen2017 native pages7/9 longitudinal and centre models

WHO.source: WHO Guidance on Research Methods for Health Emergency and Disaster Risk Management,2021 Chapter4.3
WHO.scope: Group delivery, feasibility, spillover, recruitment bias and clustered analysis; no claim that clusters are always preferable.

Jakobsen.scope: Repeated measurements and hierarchical centre effects; no automatic random-effect rule for few centres.
